title: 27-Layer Chirped Defect-Cavity Filter with Linear Quarter-Wave Scaling
scientific_hypothesis: Expanding from 25 to 27 layers with deterministic linear chirp initialization (0.8x to 1.2x quarter-wave optical thickness across stack depth) will enable broader stopband suppression in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm regions while maintaining ≥0.95 transmittance at 1550 nm, because additional DBR pairs increase stopband width and chirp breaks periodicity to suppress secondary transmission peaks.
design_principle: Defective DBR bandpass structure (HL)^N D(LH)^N with N=6 pairs per side plus central half-wave cavity, initialized with linear chirp schedule scaling quarter-wave target from 0.8x at layer 1 to 1.2x at layer 27, then optimized via gradient-based thickness search.
proposed_topology: exactly 5 alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 pairs, one cavity layer, and exactly 5 reverse-order pairs (21 finite layers)
manufacturing_considerations: chirped thicknesses may require enhanced deposition monitoring
Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair well-established for 1550 nm applications
theory_basis: Defective DBR structure (HL)^N D(LH)^N creates transmission peak at defect resonance wavelength
Linear chirp breaks strict periodicity to broaden stopband and suppress side lobes
Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda0/4 maximizes reflectance per pair for DBR mirrors
expected_advantages: 2 additional layers provide extra stopband suppression degrees of freedom
Chirp initialization explores non-quarter-wave design space more systematically
May achieve wider effective stopband than uniform 25L designs
known_risks: Chirped designs may be more sensitive to thickness errors
Optimizer may converge to local minima different from 25L baseline
execution_request_english: Design a 27-layer defective DBR bandpass filter on Fused Silica substrate with Air incident medium using Ta2O5 (high index) and SiO2 (low index). Layer sequence: Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5 (cavity), SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2. Initialize thicknesses using linear chirp: layer k thickness = quarter_wave_1550nm * (0.8 + 0.4*(k-1)/26) where quarter_wave_1550nm for Ta2O5 is lambda0/(4*n_Ta2O5) and for SiO2 is lambda0/(4*n_SiO2), cavity layer (layer 15, Ta2O5) initialized at half-wave optical thickness. Optimize all 27 thicknesses with bounds 50-350 nm for mirror layers, 400-700 nm for cavity. Evaluate coherent TMM transmittance at normal incidence, unpolarized. Target wavelengths: maximize at 1550 nm, suppress in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 5 alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 pairs, one cavity layer, and exactly 5 reverse-order pairs (21 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Increased layer count from 25 to 27 to expand stopband suppression degrees of freedom; introduced deterministic linear chirp initialization (0.8x to 1.2x scaling) per insight appendage recommendation to explore non-quarter-wave design space systematically while preserving defect-cavity scientific principle.
